headline: High-risk compliance and data-flow mismatch: Plane can ingest files and egress broadly while godot_rl_agents is local-only and non-runnable, creating default leakage and downstream-action risks.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: A has no shared channel or I/O surfaces beyond none, while B can accept file uploads and process notes/issues. The only plausible bridge is manual copy-paste or uploaded content, so injection is possible but not default. Because A is game-playing and B is email-scheduling/issue-tracking, the interaction is indirect and limited.
conditions: IF the operator copies A-generated text into B issue fields or uploads A-produced files to B
IF B treats uploaded file contents as instructions rather than data
mitigations: Disable copy-paste of untrusted A output into B
Use a fixed template for B issue text
Strip instructions from uploaded files before import
Mark A outputs as data-only in the workflow

B_data_leakage.rationale: B has broad network egress and file-upload surfaces, so it can transmit touched files and notes off-box by default. A is local-only with no network egress and no data classes touched, so it is not itself a leakage source. The pair still creates a default leakage path if A-produced artifacts are uploaded into B or if B handles sensitive files.
conditions: IF A-produced artifacts contain sensitive content and are uploaded into B
IF B forwards file contents or notes to external services over its broad egress
mitigations: Do not upload sensitive A artifacts into B
Restrict B to non-sensitive projects
Review B outbound integrations before use
Use a local-only staging folder for transfers
requires-engineering: add DLP or egress allowlisting

C_capability_conflict.rationale: A has no write or network capabilities exposed, while B explicitly cannot write the filesystem and supports multiple instances. That makes direct write-write conflict unlikely. The remaining overlap is read-only or manual handoff, so conflict risk is small and not default.
conditions: IF an external orchestrator gives both agents write access not shown in the profiles
IF B is extended with filesystem write privileges
mitigations: Keep both agents on separate workspaces
Avoid granting B filesystem write access
Run only one instance of B per shared project
Document manual handoff boundaries

D_cascading_error.rationale: B is an email-scheduling/issue-tracking agent with file and note inputs, so it may act on A outputs if the operator forwards them. A does not verify downstream actions and has no action-taking authority, but B can still turn unverified A content into tasks or messages. The pathway exists through manual handoff, not direct automation.
conditions: IF A output is pasted into B as authoritative task text
IF B sends emails or creates issues based on unverified A content
mitigations: Require human review before B acts on A output
Tag A output as unverified in B
Use a checklist for any B action derived from A
Limit B to drafting, not sending
requires-engineering: add provenance checks between agents

E_compliance.rationale: A is open-source game-playing software with no touched data classes, while B touches issues, tasks, files, images, hyperlinks, and notes and can egress broadly. No specific residency or regulated-data mismatch is documented, so the compliance concern is limited to generic handling differences rather than a proven breach. A is not cited for residency because none is stated.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed into B's issues, files, or notes
IF B is deployed in a jurisdiction or retention regime stricter than the operator expects
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of B
Set short retention on B projects
Review B export and deletion settings
Use separate tenants for sensitive work
requires-engineering: add residency and retention controls
